claim.claim-text: a microscope objective, a sample stage (12) for holding a sample (16), a light source (20) and an illumination pattern generator (22) for illuminating the sample with an illumination pattern, a camera detector (40, 44) for detecting light from the sample collected by the microscope objective, a scanning unit (24) for moving the illumination pattern in a scanning direction across the field of view, and a control unit (42) configured to selectively operate the microscope arrangement in a normal magnification mode or in a super-magnification mode, wherein in the super-magnification mode the illumination pattern forms a linear row of diffraction limited spots, wherein a movement of an active strip-like zone across the detector is implemented by recording a first plurality of partial images of a width of X pixel rows, wherein the position of the starting pixel row is incremented in synchronism with the movement of the image of the illumination pattern on the detector so that the image of the illuminated line is located within the partial image, with the width of each partial image being larger than the width of the image of the illumination spot pattern on the detector, wherein movement of the illumination pattern across the field of view is repeated at least once after the illumination pattern has been shifted laterally by a fraction of the distance between adjacent spots to at least record a second plurality of partial images, and wherein the partial images are deconvoluted according to the known motion of the sample and the illumination pattern prior to being combined to obtain a total image of the illuminated sample surface.
2. The microscope device of claim 1, wherein the total image is filtered such that the spots are compressed around their center by a factor of 2.

3. The microscope device of claim 1 or 2, wherein in the super-magnification mode the sample is moved in a direction antiparallel to the scanning direction while the illumination pattern is moved across the field of view, and wherein in the normal magnification mode the illumination pattern preferably is a line-type pattern.

4. The microscope device of one of the preceding claims, wherein the sample (16) is illuminated with the illumination pattern via the microscope objective (18) in an epifluorecence mode, or wherein the sample is illuminated in a light sheet mode in which the illumination pattern is applied from a lateral direction which is perpendicular to the optical axis of the objective.
